title: From bouts to readiness to compete: temporal dynamics of stress, fatigue, recovery and monitoring-informed decisions in combat sports.
abstract: Combat-sport tournaments require decisions before responses to previous efforts have resolved. Detecting a change does not establish that an indicator predicts the next task or improves a decision. This Perspective proposes a task- and time-specific framework linking prior bouts, recovery time and subsequent demands through three evidentiary requirements. Responsiveness concerns reproducible changes beyond measurement error when an indicator represents a response to effort. Predictive validity concerns anticipation of a pre-specified subsequent outcome and added information beyond simpler measures. Decision utility concerns improved outcomes relative to usual practice. Indicators interpreted as current status or stable capacity need not respond to prior effort, but still require adequate measurement properties and prospective evaluation. Evidence from repeated bouts, recovery interventions, mental fatigue, sleep restriction and weight loss suggests that monitoring domains are not interchangeable. The framework retains discordant indicators, evaluates combinations and communicates uncertainty without global clearance labels. Three hypotheses address task and time dependence, maintained performance with increasing effort cost, and indicator-informed decisions. Medical decisions remain independent and take precedence. This is an operational extension of existing principles, not a validated predictive tool.

title: Ask the experts: a practitioner-centred approach to resilience in emergency medical services.
abstract: Background: Resilience in high-stress occupations is commonly framed as a trait, an outcome, or the absence of psychopathology. None of these framings captures what practitioners in emergency medical services actually do, and interventions built on trait-based models have produced weak or inconsistent effects.Objective: This study argues that frontline resilience in emergency medical services is better understood as a domain-specific expert skill, and that work mode - a deliberately entered state, akin to an athlete's game face, in which the demands of the task rather than the emotional force of the scene govern functioning - is its central empirical signature. The aims were to identify factors that intensify traumatic impact, characterise the strategies practitioners use to maintain functioning, and explore systemic and relational barriers that constrain coping.Method: Twenty Queensland Ambulance Service paramedics and dispatchers (tenure 2-38 years) participated in semi-structured interviews, analysed via reflexive thematic analysis.Results: Three intensifiers of traumatic impact (unpredictability, moral weight, personal threat) defined the operational demands against which resilience was enacted. Three coping themes (baseline buffers, work mode, social scaffolding) described the architecture of sustained functioning. Work mode exhibited the defining features of skilled performance: domain specificity, a phased temporal structure (preparation, containment, recovery), and a developmental trajectory from effortful to automatic execution. Two further themes (organisational distrust, the outsider gap) described the systemic and relational conditions that constrain coping.Conclusions: Treating resilience as expertise shifts the field from descriptive stressor-outcome accounts towards assessable, trainable capacities, and exposes the limitations of trait-based self-report measures that cannot distinguish genuine resilience from unsustainable stoicism.

title: Spatial transcriptomics in immune-mediated necrotising myopathy uncovers a specific necrotic signature related to immune-driven fibrosis.
abstract: Immune-mediated necrotising myopathies (IMNM) are characterised by muscle fibre necrosis, complement deposits around non-necrotic fibres, and macrophage infiltrates. Patients experience muscle damage with fibro-fatty replacement, leading to poor strength recovery, but the pathogenesis remains unclear. To investigate IMNM pathogenesis, we applied spatial transcriptomics on myositis muscle biopsies and integrated the results with published single-nucleus transcriptomic data. This combined approach enabled analysis of gene expression with spatial localisation in the muscle. Inflammatory, fibrotic, regenerative, and lipid metabolism-related signatures were identified in IMNM, distinct from other myositis, with specific distribution in necrotic and peri-necrotic regions. A unique subtype of immune-driven fibroblasts expressing SFRP4 was enriched in IMNM necrotic areas. These cells carried a strong proportion of IMNM-enriched pathological signatures, notably a complement-linked 'tumour-like' inflammatory fibroblast signature and a specific interferon response, characterised by the expression of metallothioneins. Peri-necrotic areas were characterised by pathological muscle signatures carrying interferon response and FABP4+ metabolically dysfunctional signatures. In conclusion, IMNM necrotic muscle areas are linked to a specific SFRP4-expressing fibroblast subtype interacting with macrophages, potentially driving the pathological muscle phenotype and contributing to inflammation, fibro-fatty replacement, and strength loss.

title: Sleep Management in Paralympic Sports: Knowledge, Monitoring Practices, and Perceived Barriers among Coaches and Healthcare Staff.
abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Coaches and healthcare staff play a crucial role in disseminating knowledge about the importance of sleep to develop a precise balance between recovery and the demands imposed by sports training.
OBJECTIVES: To assess the knowledge on sleep, jet lag, and sleep hygiene (SH) among coaches and healthcare staff in Paralympic sports; 2) to identify whether the sleep of Paralympic athletes is monitored, and which instruments are commonly used; and 3) to identify the main barriers faced in sleep management.
MATERIALS AND METHODS: The present cross-sectional study was conducted with 60 coaches and healthcare staff who work in the preparation of elite Paralympic athletes. The participants filled out the Sleep Beliefs Scale and a structured questionnaire before traveling to the 2020 Tokyo Paralympic Games.
RESULTS: Coaches and healthcare staff understand the importance of sleep for sports performance and recovery, but only 56% monitored their sleep. The most commonly used methods were subjective. Lack of adherence and commitment among Paralympic athletes (27%) and lack of training (19%) were the main barriers to sleep management.
CONCLUSION: Coaches and healthcare staff are aware of the importance of sleep; however, educational programs are needed to improve the training of coaching and healthcare staff for efficient sleep management and to raise awareness among Paralympic athletes about the importance of sleep.

title: Statistical Parametric Mapping reveals sex-specific, phase-dependent differences in bilateral three-dimensional ground reaction force during Wushu Changbing PiJi in high-level athletes.
abstract: PiJi is a core attacking technique in Wushu Changbing competition, but continuous waveform evidence remains limited regarding the sex-specific phase characteristics of bilateral 3D ground reaction force (GRF) during PiJi performed with maximal voluntary effort (MVE). This study aimed to compare continuous changes in trailing-foot, lead-foot, and net bilateral GRF between high-level male and female athletes during PiJi performed with MVE. In this cross-sectional, laboratory-based observational study, 44 right-hand-dominant athletes, including 22 male athletes and 22 female athletes, performed PiJi with MVE, yielding 616 valid trials. Bilateral 3D GRF was recorded using two force plates. Each trial was time-normalized and linearly interpolated to 143 equally spaced nodes, and within-participant mean waveforms were calculated before between-group differences were analyzed using statistical parametric mapping. Primary analyses used random-field-theory inference, with sensitivity examined using 5,000 permutation tests. After Bonferroni correction, phase-specific sex differences were detected in trailing-foot, lead-foot, and net bilateral 3D GRF. Scalar localization showed that male athletes had higher trailing-foot Fy during the middle phase (33.98%-47.04%) and higher trailing-foot Fx (62.41%-71.99%) and net bilateral Fx (54.18%-70.41%) during the middle-to-late phase; female athletes showed only a brief period of higher trailing-foot vertical Fz during the middle phase (42.11%-44.61%). Although lead-foot 3D GRF differed overall, no confirmatory difference was localized to any single scalar component. These findings indicate that sex-related GRF differences in high-level PiJi were concentrated mainly in specific horizontal-plane phases of trailing-foot and net bilateral force, whereas the lead-foot difference was identified only at the overall 3D GRF level. These results provide kinetic evidence for phase-specific assessment of PiJi technique and suggest that training monitoring and mechanistic research should consider foot, direction, and movement phase rather than relying only on peak force or discrete variables. Future studies integrating multimodal measures and sport-specific performance may further clarify the functional significance of bilateral force-generation patterns.

title: Feasibility of a community-based physical activity programme in individuals with Long Covid: insights from the Hertfordshire longitudinal observational programme.
abstract: This study explores the feasibility of implementing and evaluating a community-based physical activity programme for individuals with Long Covid in Hertfordshire, UK. Long Covid presents unique challenges including fluctuating symptoms, post-exertional malaise and difficulties with re-engagement following symptom flare-ups. Developed collaboratively by the Herts Sports & Physical Activity Partnership and local NHS Covid Rehabilitation Services, the programme aimed to address these challenges through tailored physical activity opportunities informed by the lived experience of Long Covid. A longitudinal observational design was used to evaluate programme retention, symptom severity, health-related quality of life and physical activity levels among 62 participants over a 12-month period. Data were collected via validated self-report tools including the EQ-5D-5L, EQ-VAS, SBQ-LC and VAS pain scale. High initial engagement was observed, with 89% of participants completing the first follow-up survey and 52% remaining engaged through to follow-up 4. While average physical activity minutes remained stable, the proportion of inactive participants declined from 37% to 25%. Statistically significant improvements were observed in self-rated health (EQ-VAS), breathing difficulties, fatigue and brain fog. Weak but significant correlations were found between increased physical activity and reduced symptom severity in several domains, including mobility, self-care and musculoskeletal pain. No significant changes were observed in anxiety or depression, suggesting physical activity alone may not address the full spectrum of Long Covid symptoms. These findings demonstrate that community-based physical activity interventions are feasible for people with Long Covid, though sustained behavioural change and mental health support remain important challenges. This study contributes practical insights for service development while highlighting the need for more rigorous controlled designs and diverse sampling in future research.

title: A two-factor framework to assess international male field hockey movement characteristics: Implications for performance preparation.
abstract: We aimed to establish the nature and structure of the relationships between high-intensity movement characteristics during international field hockey matches. Global positioning system data were obtained from 28 elite male field hockey players (n = 393 international player-matches). Mean and 90% trimmed range were extracted for the 10 most intense 1-min periods (separated by >60s) for: total distance (m); high-speed distance (>5 m·s-1); sprint distance (>7 m·s-1); accelerations (>2.5 m·s-2); decelerations (<-2.5 m·s-2) and high-speed cuts (>45° change-of-direction at >5 m·s-1). Pearson's correlations were calculated for pairs of characteristics (summed across the 10 most intense periods). An exploratory factor analysis was then applied to movement characteristics. Finally, factors were validated by testing whether they discriminated between playing positions using random-effect linear-mixed models. Factor analysis explained 76% of total variance (χ42 = 286, p < 0.001) and resulted in a two-factor solution: 'Distance' (total, high-speed and sprint distance), and 'Acceleration' (accelerations and decelerations). High-speed cuts loaded onto both factors. The two factors also discriminated significantly between playing positions. Our data-driven approach indicates that Distance and Acceleration are distinct factors of international male field hockey, specifically, Midfielders cover more distance than Defenders, and Strikers change speed and direction more than Midfielders or Defenders. Practitioners should consider prescribing and monitoring these distinct factors separately.

title: Aerobic exercise preconditioning enhances skeletal muscle resistance and recovery after contusion: involvement of the SIRT1/PGC-1α axis.
abstract:
OBJECTIVE: Compared with passive recovery after injury, exercise preconditioning may provide an active strategy for improving the subsequent response of skeletal muscle to injury. This study aimed to investigate the effects of aerobic exercise preconditioning (AEP) on skeletal muscle injury (SMI) and post-injury repair, with particular focus on the involvement of the SIRT1/PGC-1α axis and changes in PGC-1α acetylation.
METHODS: This study initially investigated the effects of continuous aerobic exercise on skeletal muscle in healthy mice. Subsequently, the influence of AEP on injury severity and regenerative repair of the gastrocnemius muscle was examined in mice with SMI. Western blotting was used to determine the expression levels of SIRT1 and PGC-1α proteins, immunoprecipitation was performed to assess the acetylation status of PGC-1α, and qRT-PCR was used to analyze the expression of genes associated with mitochondrial biogenesis-related markers and muscle regeneration. Finally, the involvement of SIRT1 signaling in the AEP-associated response to SMI was further examined using the pharmacological SIRT1 inhibitor EX527.
RESULTS: Continuous aerobic exercise was associated with increased SIRT1/PGC-1α signaling and changes in mitochondrial biogenesis-related markers in the gastrocnemius muscle of healthy mice. AEP was associated with reduced injury-related changes and an improved post-injury repair profile in mice with SMI. During the early stage after injury, AEP was accompanied by sustained SIRT1/ PGC-1α signaling and reduced PGC-1α acetylation. Pharmacological inhibition of SIRT1 with EX527 partially attenuated the AEP-associated protective and reparative effects on the injured gastrocnemius muscle.
CONCLUSION: These findings suggest that AEP establishes an adaptive state in skeletal muscle that is associated with reduced injury-related damage and an enhanced post-injury reparative response. The SIRT1/PGC-1α axis and altered PGC-1α acetylation may contribute to these AEP-associated effects.

title: Beyond movement behaviours: Unravelling the prospective links between 24-hour behavioural composition and affective dynamics in adolescent athletes.
abstract:
BACKGROUND: While the full spectrum of 24-h movement behaviours - encompassing sleep (SLP), screen-based sedentary behaviour (Screen-SB), light physical activity (LPA), structured moderate-to-vigorous physical activity (S-MVPA), and unstructured moderate-to-vigorous physical activity (US-MVPA) - is consistently linked to daily affective states in adolescent athletes, existing literature has rarely examined these behaviours as an interdependent time-use composition, and largely fails to disentangle the distinct effects of structured versus unstructured MVPA subdomains on emotional outcomes.
MATERIALS AND METHODS: Using a repeated-measures prospective daily design, this study included 161 adolescent athletes (101 males and 60 females). Accelerometers were used to quantify 24-h movement behaviours. Four affective dimensions were assessed through ecological momentary assessment (EMA): high-arousal positive affect, low-arousal positive affect, high-arousal negative affect, and low-arousal negative affect. Bayesian multilevel compositional models were used to estimate between- and within-person associations, while isotemporal substitution analyses evaluated the estimated effects of reallocating time between behaviours on next-day affect.
RESULTS: Associations between 24-h behaviour compositions and next-day affect were more evident at the within-person level. A higher relative proportion of LPA was associated with higher high-arousal positive affect (0.305, 95% Bayesian credible interval [CrI] 0.255 to 0.354) and low-arousal positive affect (0.292, 95% CrI 0.245 to 0.338), and lower high-arousal negative affect (-0.231, 95% CrI -0.260 to -0.203) and low-arousal negative affect (-0.210, 95% CrI -0.236 to -0.185). In 30-min substitution analyses, reallocating time from other behaviours to LPA generally showed more favourable associations with next-day affect at both between- and within-person levels, although the associations varied across substitution pairs and affective dimensions. These findings highlight LPA as the behaviour most consistently associated with favourable next-day affect.
CONCLUSIONS: Daily 24-h movement behaviour composition was prospectively associated with next-day affect in adolescent athletes. LPA showed the most consistent favourable associations with next-day affect, particularly when replacing SB. Promoting LPA may represent a feasible strategy for supporting affective wellbeing without adding to existing training demands.

title: Task Force 8: Care of Competitive Athletes with Arrhythmias and Sudden Cardiac Arrest: Clinical Considerations and Electrocardiogram Interpretations.
abstract: This document outlines recommendations for managing competitive athletes with arrhythmias and risks of sudden cardiac arrest, emphasizing individualized risk assessment, shared decision-making, and return-to-play protocols tailored to each athlete's cardiac profile and sport demands. It provides evaluation strategies for ventricular arrhythmias, implantable cardiac defibrillators, atrial fibrillation, supraventricular tachycardia, Wolff-Parkinson-White pattern/syndrome, and syncope, alongside guidance for electrocardiogram interpretation in athletes. A key focus is placed on differentiating between low-risk and high-risk conditions, with recommendations for treatment strategies and ongoing monitoring to ensure athletes' safety.

title: Running the Numbers: High Metabolic Load Distance as an Alternative to Traditional External Load Metrics in Elite Women's Football.
abstract: This study examined the relationship between High Metabolic Load Distance (HMLD) and both session RPE (sRPE) and athlete wellness in women's football and compared it with traditional load monitoring metrics. An observational design was used to collect data from one elite women's football team during training and games in the 2024/25 A-League W season. Twenty-four athletes wore global positioning devices to capture external load metrics, including total distance (TD), high-speed running distance (HSRD) and HMLD. Session RPE and daily wellness were collected through online questionnaires. Generalised additive models were used to examine non-linear relationships between external load, subsequent days' wellness and RPE, and relationships between morning wellness and same-day external load. Higher load was associated with increased sRPE, and poorer next-day wellness, with effects diminishing within two to 3 days post-session. Across all outcomes, HMLD demonstrated stronger and more consistent relationships than TD and HSRD, explaining a greater proportion of variance in wellness and sRPE. Same-day wellness was associated with differences in distances, with higher motivation and lower fatigue corresponding to higher HMLD. HMLD demonstrated comparatively stronger associations with immediate perceived exertion and short-term athlete reported wellness than traditional distance-based metrics in this cohort. These findings support the application of HMLD as a practical and sensitive measure to inform training decision-making in elite women's football.

title: Shoulder Arthritis.
abstract: Glenohumeral osteoarthritis is a common, debilitating joint disease characterized by progressive cartilage loss, subchondral bone remodeling, and capsular stiffness, leading to pain, restricted motion, and functional impairment. Diagnosis relies on both clinical evaluation and imaging studies. Classification systems, such as the Walch classification, assist in assessing disease severity and guiding treatment decisions. Management begins with conservative approaches, including nonsteroidal anti-inflammatory drugs (NSAIDs), physical therapy, and intra-articular injections, progressing to surgical interventions such as total or reverse shoulder arthroplasty for advanced disease. Early diagnosis and patient-specific treatment are essential to ensuring optimal patient outcomes.

title: Bilateral insufficiency fractures of the femoral condyles after discontinuation of glucocorticoid therapy for ulcerative colitis: A case report.
abstract: Glucocorticoid therapy is a well-established risk factor for osteoporosis and insufficiency fractures. However, insufficiency fractures developing after discontinuation of glucocorticoid therapy have been infrequently described. We present a case of bilateral insufficiency fractures of the femoral condyles detected approximately one year after discontinuation of glucocorticoid therapy in a patient with ulcerative colitis. A 53-year-old man presented with progressive bilateral knee pain without antecedent trauma. He had previously received glucocorticoid therapy for ulcerative colitis, including oral prednisolone and budesonide. The last course had been discontinued approximately one year before symptom onset. Physical examination revealed bilateral weight-bearing pain with mild swelling but without redness or restriction of motion. Laboratory findings showed no inflammatory response, and plain X-rays showed no abnormalities. Magnetic resonance imaging revealed bilateral bone marrow edema and fracture lines in the femoral condyles, consistent with bilateral insufficiency fractures. Dual-energy X-ray absorptiometry confirmed osteoporosis, with T-scores of -2.4 at the lumbar spine and -3.3 at the femoral neck, and trabecular bone score was 1.171, suggesting that the trabecular microarchitecture was markedly degraded. He was treated with temporary non-weight-bearing rehabilitation and daily administration of abaloparatide. Knee pain gradually improved, and follow-up magnetic resonance imaging demonstrated resolution of signal abnormalities. Bone mineral density showed modest improvement, although trabecular bone score remained in the degraded range. In patients with a history of glucocorticoid exposure, bone fragility persists even after discontinuation of glucocorticoid therapy, and ongoing evaluation and treatment for osteoporosis are necessary.

title: Superimposed tendon vibration during brief voluntary submaximal knee extensions does not modulate corticospinal excitability in healthy adults.
abstract: Superimposed local vibration (SLV) provides additional proprioceptive input during voluntary contractions, but its influence on corticospinal and motoneuronal responsiveness during visually matched force task remains unclear. Previous work at low contraction intensity reported unchanged corticospinal responses, but whether SLV alters motoneuronal responsiveness across submaximal contraction intensities remains unknown. Accordingly, we examined corticospinal and thoracic evoked responses in twenty-one participants performing 6-s force-matched knee extensions with visual feedback at 30%, 50%, and 70% of maximal voluntary isometric contraction. Brief contractions were performed either under control conditions (CON) or with superimposed local vibration (SLV) applied to the quadriceps tendon (100 Hz, 2 - 3 mm). For each condition and intensity, evoked responses were recorded from the vastus lateralis and rectus femoris during 18 contractions, including two peripheral nerve stimulations to evoke maximal M-waves (MMAX), ten transcranial magnetic stimulations to evoke motor-evoked potentials (MEPs), and six thoracic electrical stimulations to evoke thoracic motor-evoked potentials (TMEPs). MEPs and TMEPs were matched to 25 - 35% of MMAX, and peak-to-peak amplitudes and response areas were analyzed.

title: Clonal articular cartilage progenitors outperform mesenchymal stromal cells in mitigating post-traumatic osteoarthritis.
abstract:
OBJECTIVE: This study aimed to compare the functional, pathological, and immunomodulatory properties of articular chondroprogenitors (ACPs) with those of bone-marrow-derived mesenchymal stromal cells (MSCs) in preventing the progression of post-traumatic osteoarthritis (PTOA) after destabilization of the medial meniscus (DMM) injury in a mouse model.
METHOD: ACP and MSC were isolated from three horses and assessed for their immunomodulatory capacity in vitro. Aliquots of selected ACP clones and MSCs were injected intra-articularly into male mice 1-week post destabilization of the medial meniscus (DMM). The functional mobility of the mice before the injury and at weeks 2, 4, and 8 post-injury was assessed by two methods: ANY-maze™ voluntary mobility monitoring and DigiGait™ compulsory gait analysis. Upon euthanasia, joints were collected for histological scoring.
RESULTS: In vitro assessments demonstrated that ACPs and MSCs had anti-inflammatory properties: both treatments produced lower levels of pro-inflammatory cytokines, while only the ACPs produced more anti-inflammatory cytokines than controls. In vivo, both ACPs and MSCs lessened the effects of DMM on mobility. Histological scoring revealed significant reductions of PTOA in the medial compartment with ACPs relative to both MSCs and vehicle controls. Overall, ACPs effectively reduced PTOA progression to a greater extent than MSCs.
CONCLUSION: Our findings demonstrated that both equine ACP and MSC treatments provided symptom modification over vehicle controls in a short-term animal study. Notably, ACPs may be more efficacious than MSCs at reducing structural joint pathology.

title: Sports Trauma in Athletes with Impairment.
abstract:
PURPOSE OF REVIEW: Trauma in athletes with impairment is an under-reported aspect of Para sport. This review article aims to present current data regarding characteristics of acute sports trauma in winter and summer Para sport participants and considerations for management of acute injury. This includes recommendations for trauma prevention and preparedness, assessment and management on the field of play, and extrication from Para sport equipment.
RECENT FINDINGS: Injury surveillance systems help characterize risk factors for acute sports trauma and inform injury prevention programs. Concussion and injuries to the head and face are common in Para sport. Winter sports such as Para alpine skiing and sled hockey have high rates of acute sports trauma. While summer sports generally have higher rates of repetitive use injuries, some sports such as blind football, Para cycling, wheelchair rugby, judo, and goalball have higher rates of acute traumatic injuries. There are many important factors to consider when assessing field of play, extrication, emergency evaluation, and care-coordination considerations. title: Patient-Reported Outcomes Plateau at 1 Year Compared With 2 Years After Open Proximal Hamstring Repair.
abstract:
PURPOSE: To determine whether there is a significant difference between 1- and 2-year postoperative patient-reported outcome measures (PROMs) after proximal hamstring repair (PHR).
METHODS: This retrospective study used data from an institutional registry of patients who underwent PHR between October 2021 and December 2023 with a minimum follow-up of 24 months. Patients who completed preoperative and 1- and 2-year postoperative surveys were included in this study. PROMs included the Lower Extremity Functional Scale, the Hip Outcome Score, the Perth Hamstring Assessment, and the 12-Item Short Form Survey. Cohort-specific minimal clinically important difference was calculated. Return to sport and surgical satisfaction were included as secondary outcomes. Univariate analyses compared clinical outcomes.
RESULTS: Sixty-two of 84 eligible patients met the inclusion criteria for this study, with a mean follow-up time of 23.2 months (range 22.4-24.8). No significant differences were found between 1- and 2-year PROMs after PHR (P > .05). There were no statistically significant differences in the proportion of patients who achieved minimal clinically important difference at 1 year versus 2 years postoperatively, and these differences remained nonsignificant after disaggregating the data by sex (P > .05). After 1 year postoperatively, there were no significant additional improvements in the ability to return to sport (P = .371), sport level (P > .99), or percentage of return to sport (P = .961).
CONCLUSIONS: No significant differences were found between 1- and 2-year PROMs after PHR. PROM scores, minimal clinically important difference achievement rates, return to sport, and surgical satisfaction outcomes were stable from 1 to 2 years postoperatively, with no clinically meaningful improvements observed in the second postoperative year.
LEVEL OF EVIDENCE: Level IV, retrospective case series.

title: Understanding Sleep in Ultramarathon Runners: An Exploratory Assessment during a Training Week.
abstract: Sleep plays a vital role in sports performance. Ultramarathon runners may experience impaired sleep during training and competition; however, further investigation is needed. The current study aimed to evaluate sleep in ultramarathon runners during a typical training week. We evaluated 15 male athletes with a mean age of 45.1 ± 10.5 years and a mean ultramarathon experience of 6.37 ± 6.49 years. Sleep was assessed using the Munich Chronotype Questionnaire, the Morningness-Eveningness Questionnaire, the Pittsburgh Sleep Quality Index, the Athlete Sleep Behavior Questionnaire, the Epworth Sleepiness Scale, and a 7-day sleep diary. Most participants were morning chronotypes (86.7%), and the mean social jetlag of was 0.60 ± 0.69 hour. The athletes went to bed and woke up earlier on workdays than on free days ( p = 0.002). Most athletes reported < 8 hours of sleep per night, 53.3% reported poor sleep-related behaviors, and 46.7% were classified as poor sleepers; however, 73.3% did not report excessive daytime sleepiness. These findings suggest a heterogeneous and multidimensional sleep-health profile in ultramarathon runners.

title: Voluntary wheel running attenuates mechanical hypersensitivity but transiently prolongs gait impairments in male and female mice with unilateral osteoarthritis.
abstract:
OBJECTIVE: Physical activity is a first-line therapeutic intervention for managing osteoarthritis-related pain and functional impairment. However, the growing literature questions the long-term relevance of exercise-induced improvements in patients, while pre-clinical research evidence-base is limited by reliance on stressful, forced exercise paradigms which do not reflect voluntary engagement. Here, we investigated the effects of voluntary wheel running on the pain experience in mice with joint pain.
DESIGN: We investigated the impact of free access to a running wheel on sensory, functional and affective outcomes following unilateral intra-articular injection of monoiodoacetate (MIA) into the knee joint of 8-week-old male and female C57Bl/6J mice (n=14/16). Mice were single-housed and randomly assigned to remain sedentary or have unrestricted access to a wheel from at least two weeks before MIA. Behavioural outcomes were assessed longitudinally over an eight-week post-injection period.
RESULTS: Mean daily running distance decreased from 3.01 to 0.69 km in males and from 3.90 to 1.69 km in females by day 5 after MIA. Following a short-lived recovery, males showed a progressive decline, while the rebound in activity was sustained in females throughout the observation period. Voluntary wheel running attenuated MIA-induced secondary mechanical hypersensitivity, with higher mechanical withdrawal thresholds in active than sedentary mice, most obviously during the pain-like maintenance stage (day 40: males: 0.08g; 95%CI 0.040 to 0.126; females: 0.125g, 95%CI 0.029 to 0.222). Conversely, wheel running transiently delayed full gait recovery, with between-group differences in stance symmetry and duty factor during early recovery in both sexes (males day 20: stance: -11.8%; 95%CI -21.25 to -2.27; duty factor: -5.4%; 95%CI -10.53 to -0.35; females day 12: stance: -22.0%; 95%CI -32.48 to -11.51; duty factor: -15.9%; 95%CI -22.97 to -8.83). Finally, wheel access had little effect on anxio-depressive-like behaviours or cognition, but reduced faecal output and influenced body weight.
CONCLUSIONS: In this animal model of MIA-induced osteoarthritis, voluntary wheel running was associated with improvements in secondary mechanical hypersensitivity, despite a transient and acute worsening of several gait impairments. These findings highlight the importance of assessing multiple behavioural domains in preclinical studies and underscore the complexity of exercise-induced effects on pain and function.

title: Delayed Diagnosis of Achilles Tendon Rupture in a 75-Year-Old Patient with Bimalleolar Ankle Fracture: A Case Report.
abstract:
CASE: A 75-year-old woman sustained a minimally displaced bimalleolar ankle fracture after a fall. An ipsilateral Achilles tendon rupture was missed until day 26, when persistent heel pain and inability to plantarflex prompted an MRI, revealing a rupture with a 5.5-cm gap. Both injuries were treated nonoperatively using controlled ankle motion (CAM) boots, heel wedges, progressive weight bearing, and rehabilitation. At 12 months, the patient had resumed independent ambulation.
CONCLUSION: All ankle fracture patients should undergo systematic Achilles tendon assessment with early follow-up reassessment and a low threshold for advanced imaging when the initial examination is limited.

title: The Sleep and Diet of Elite Female Australian Rules Football Athletes Differ With Age and Season Phase.
abstract: The Australian Football League Women's (AFLW) competition is comprised of a short, intensive competitive season, highlighting the importance of proper fuelling and recovery to support performance. Little is known about the dietary and sleep habits of AFLW athletes across a season, and the influence that age has on these behaviours. Therefore, this study aimed to determine the effects of season phase and age on dietary intake and sleep in elite AFLW athletes. Dietary intake and sleep were assessed in 22 AFLW athletes (25.9 ± 5.0 y) over 10 nights, including five consecutive nights during both pre-season and in-season. Dietary intake was quantified through self-reported food diaries using a smartphone application (Easy Diet Diary), and sleep via a wearable monitoring device (Oura ring). Restricted maximum likelihood mixed models were used to determine variations in dietary intake and sleep in AFLW players between season phases (i.e., pre-season vs. in-season) and age. In-season protein (115.15 ± 35.14 vs. 126.48 ± 40.10 g, p = 0.026) and fat intakes (72.93 ± 29.55 vs. 83.43 ± 33.14 g, p = 0.012) were significantly lower compared to pre-season, with no differences in sleep measures observed between season phases. While age did not influence dietary intake, each additional year of age was associated with 8 min less sleep (p = 0.001) and 4 min earlier wake times (p = 0.032). These findings suggest that protein and fat intakes fluctuate across the seasons, with increasing age being a non-modifiable risk factor for shorter sleep durations within AFLW athletes.

title: Gender Differences in Sports Injuries of the Foot and Ankle.
abstract: This article examines sex-based differences in foot and ankle injuries among female athletes, emphasizing the role of anatomic, hormonal, biomechanical, and sociocultural factors. Female athletes are disproportionately affected by ankle sprains, chronic instability, and bone stress injuries. Conditions such as relative energy deficiency in sport and the female athlete triad contribute to injury risk and long-term health consequences but remain under-recognized. This article highlights disparities in research, treatment, and outcomes, calling for improved screening, sex-specific prevention strategies, and greater inclusion of female subjects in sports medicine research to inform evidence-based care and optimize outcomes for female athletes.

title: The fate of poised pre-mRNAs shapes mitochondrial activity and cellular differentiation.
abstract: Although RNA quality control tightly regulates gene expression, the scope of its regulatory functions in the nucleus remains unclear. In this study, we describe the quality control, on chromatin, of poised intron-containing polyadenylated RNAs (PIA-RNAs). Whether these precursor messenger RNAs (pre-mRNAs) constitute immature mRNAs whose splicing is pending or, alternatively, are degraded by the nuclear RNA exosome depends on whether they engage nuclear cap-binding protein 3 (NCBP3) or anillin, respectively. Many PIA-RNAs inversely controlled by NCBP3 and anillin encode mitochondrial factors. Thus, NCBP3 depletion in mouse as well as pathogenic mutations in the RNA exosome in humans result in reduced mitochondrial activity, muscle weakness, cerebellar hypomyelination, and diminished motor coordination. Our findings reveal a competition between pre-mRNA metabolic pathways whose balance controls mitochondrial function and, when perturbed, leads to neurological diseases.

title: "Becoming a Person Again": A Qualitative Study of Personal Recovery Experiences Following a Supervised Exercise Programme in Treatment-Resistant Depression.
abstract: This study explored how individuals with treatment-resistant depression (TRD), experienced and interpreted changes following a supervised combined exercise programme. A qualitative study was conducted within the TRACE-RMD trial. Twenty-four adults with TRD who completed a 12-week supervised combined exercise programme, integrating aerobic interval and resistance training at individually prescribed intensities, participated in individual semi-structured interviews, which were conducted face to face and analysed using reflexive thematic analysis. The participants described exercise as a meaningful context for interconnected changes extending beyond physical fitness and depressive symptoms. Four overarching themes were identified: (1) re-engaging with the body; (2) regaining psychological agency; (3) reclaiming everyday life; and (4) "becoming a person" again. The participants described immediate experiences during sessions alongside more enduring changes in daily life, including greater physical confidence, renewed agency, re-engagement with everyday routines, social connection, and a stronger sense of self. Supervised exercise may support personal recovery in people with TDR not only by improving physical and psychological health but also by facilitating behavioural activation, social reconnection, and reconstruction of identity. These findings suggest that the value of supervised exercise may lie not only in its effects on the health condition, but also in the opportunities it creates for meaningful change within multidisciplinary mental health care.

title: Gene amplification during differentiation of mesenchymal stem cells towards chondrocytes.
abstract: For decades, gene amplification was described as an attribute of tumor cells and as a physiological mechanism to increase gene copy numbers for the higher protein demand during the development of amphibians and flies. Notably, gene amplification has since been detected in normal mammalian cells during differentiation. Numerous amplified genes detected in tumor cells overlap with amplified genes detected during stem cell differentiation. Since stem cells have a valuable potency in regenerative therapies and since cartilage regeneration is a highly demanded therapeutic strategy, the current study investigated gene amplification dynamics during the chondrogenic differentiation of human mesenchymal stem cells (hMSCs). Using quantitative PCR, copy number changes were analyzed for genes previously implicated in differentiation, as well as genes amplified in chondrosarcoma, including CDK4, MDM2, AGAP2, CPT1B, SHANK3, TRIB1 and MYC. Amplifications were transient and stage-specific: CDK4, CPT1B and SHANK3 exhibited the highest copy number increases at day 2, followed by a gradual decline by day 7, whereas AGAP2 and MDM2 increased later in differentiation. Laser microdissection of toluidine blue-stained areas revealed heterogeneity in amplification patterns: CDK4 amplification was prominent in areas lacking or showing moderate proteoglycan deposition; CPT1B amplification occurred in regions with absent, moderate or intense proteoglycan deposition; and SHANK3 amplification was restricted to areas with intense proteoglycan deposition. Notably, regions with the strongest proteoglycan staining exhibited no gene amplification, suggesting that gene amplification is an early, transient event that diminishes as differentiation progresses. These findings highlight gene amplification as a mechanism during chondrogenesis, potentially critical for early differentiation stages and genome stability in mature cells.

title: PTHrP suppresses BMP2-induced osteochondral differentiation and preserves cartilage phenotype in mesenchymal stem cells via inactivating PI3K-AKT signaling.
abstract: Bone morphogenetic protein 2 (BMP2) has the potential to drive multipotent mesenchymal stem cells (MSCs) to undergo chondral-osteogenic (including hypertrophic chondrocyte) differentiation. Parathyroid hormone-related protein (PTHrP) plays an essential role in fetal endochondral ossification, although persistent PTHrP stimulation leads to postnatal bone loss. Here, we investigated the effects of PTHrP on BMP2-induced endochondral ossification through hypertrophic chondrocyte differentiation of MSCs. We found that silencing PTHrP expression inhibited BMP2-induced chondrogenic, hypertrophic, and osteogenic differentiation of MSCs, while overexpression of PTHrP promoted BMP2-induced chondrogenic differentiation of MSCs and suppressed BMP2-induced hypertrophic differentiation of MSCs. Using stem cell implantation studies in athymic nude mice, we demonstrated that while MSCs with silenced PTHrP expression exhibited significantly reduced endochondral ossification of subcutaneous cartilage, overexpression of PTHrP promoted the growth of subcutaneous cartilage while significantly delaying ossification, leading to the preservation of cartilage phenotype. Mechanistically, we showed that exogenous PTHrP promoted BMP2-induced chondrogenic differentiation of MSCs by up-regulating Sox9 expression and inactivating PI3K-AKT signaling. Collectively, our findings strongly suggest that PTHrP may play an important role in mediating BMP2-induced chondral-osteogenic differentiation of MSCs by inactivating PI3K-AKT signaling, indicating that PTHrP may be exploited for endochondral cartilage-bone tissue engineering.

title: Ultrasound-triggered bio-scaffold integrating engineered stem cells for cartilage regeneration.
abstract: Articular cartilage repair remains a major clinical challenge due to the limited regenerative capacity of the tissue and the poor therapeutic efficacy of current treatments. Although stem cell-based therapies hold promise, their clinical outcomes are often compromised by insufficient chondrogenic differentiation, phenotypic instability, and rapid cell loss in the dynamic joint environment. Herein, we report an ultrasound-responsive, bio-scaffold system (e-BMSCs/Gel) designed to enhance cartilage regeneration through coordinated biochemical and genetic regulation. In this system, bone marrow mesenchymal stem cells (BMSCs) are engineered by internalizing nanobubbles (NBs) loaded with TGF-β3 protein and CRISPR/Cas9 plasmids targeting the YAP (pCas9-YAP), termed T@NBspDNA. Additionally, to enhance cell retention and survival, engineered BMSCs (e-BMSCs) are encapsulated within a thermosensitive thiolated-chitosan/hydroxyapatite hydrogel that rapidly forms in situ. Under US stimulation, the synchronized activation of TGF-β3 release and YAP gene silencing significantly promoted the chondrogenic differentiation of e-BMSCs. Furthermore, in vivo evaluation in a rat articular cartilage defect model demonstrates that US-activated e-BMSCs/Gel effectively promotes hyaline-like cartilage regeneration and improves structural restoration of the defect site. Overall, this work presents a controllable bio-scaffold platform, offering a novel strategy for effective cartilage regeneration.

title: Targeting the lactate/P300/H3K18la epigenetic pathway with a mechanoadaptive biomimetic hydrogel to suppress traumatic tendon heterotopic ossification.
abstract: Traumatic heterotopic ossification (HO) is a debilitating complication of tendon injury, yet its pathogenic mechanisms remain elusive and effective preventive strategies are lacking. Here, we identify a glycometabolic-epigenetic axis that drives HO progression. Single-cell profiling and functional analyses reveal that hypoxic chondrocytes undergo glycolytic reprogramming, leading to lactate accumulation and transfer into tendon-derived mesenchymal stem cells (TD-MSCs) through MCT1. This metabolic coupling promotes P300-dependent histone H3 lysine 18 lactylation (H3K18la), activating osteogenic programs characterized by Col6a1, Zhx3, Lox and Vdr expression and thereby facilitating pathological endochondral ossification. Guided by this mechanism, we develop a tendon-adhesive hydrogel (GelHA-A485@Exos) that integrates mechanical repair with targeted epigenetic modulation. MSC-derived exosomes enable localized delivery of the P300 inhibitor A485, suppressing H3K18la and aberrant osteogenic activation, while the hydrogel scaffold enhances tendon regeneration. In vivo and in vitro studies demonstrate that GelHA-A485@Exos promotes tendon healing while preventing HO formation. Our findings establish metabolic-epigenetic communication as a central regulator of traumatic HO and provide a translational therapeutic strategy for its clinical prevention.

title: Exercise-related signal abnormality (ERSA)-associated acute thigh muscle injuries in a subset of professional soccer players.
abstract:
OBJECTIVE: Exercise-related signal abnormality (ERSA) is a relatively new MRI entity described in professional soccer players. We report a subset of players who sustained acute muscle injuries and ERSA lesions in the same muscle.
MATERIALS AND METHODS: A retrospective review was conducted from July 2024 to July 2026 to identify all MRI studies of professional soccer players with an acute thigh muscle injury and ERSA lesion in the same muscle. Anatomical site, laterality, ERSA lesion subtype and length, and acute muscle injury grade as per the British Athletics Muscle Injury Classification (BAMIC) were recorded.
RESULTS: There were 18 ERSA-associated acute thigh muscle injuries in 16 soccer players (12 males, 4 females; median age 20.5 years). Affected muscles were the rectus femoris (n = 12), adductor longus (n = 5), and semitendinosus (n = 1). Type C ERSA lesions (n = 13) and BAMIC grade 2b (n = 8) muscle injuries were the most common. All acute muscle injuries were located within the ERSA lesions. No intratendinous extension was observed. Median ERSA lesion length was 21.5 cm and median acute muscle injury length was 7.0 cm. The main ERSA-associated muscle injury patterns were pre-degloving (n = 6) and myofascial (n = 6) injuries of the rectus femoris and distal myotendinous junction injuries of the adductor longus (n = 4).
CONCLUSION: We describe a new muscle injury pattern, termed ERSA-associated acute thigh muscle injuries, in a cohort of professional soccer players. Distinct injury patterns were observed in the rectus femoris and adductor longus.

title: Acute lower leg compartment syndrome as a result of calf strain due to a skiing injury.
abstract: Acute compartment syndrome (ACS) of the lower leg is a limb-threatening condition that requires urgent management. It is most commonly caused by direct trauma, such as high-speed motor vehicle accidents or blunt force injuries, including those seen in earthquake victims. Lower extremity ACS most commonly occurs in the setting of a tibial fracture. ACS can also occur as a result of non-contact injuries, such as muscle strain during athletic activities. Early clinical suspicion and close monitoring are critical, as the most telling symptom is pain. Neurovascular signs typically appear later in the progression of the condition. While imaging tools like ultrasound and MRI may help identify muscle tears and large haematomas, they are not diagnostic for ACS. When the clinical picture is unclear, compartment pressure measurement can aid diagnosis—particularly in settings where access to surgical intervention is limited and transportation decisions are challenging. We present an unusual case of ACS in the leg following a muscle injury sustained during skiing. The patient’s severe pain, along with physical findings of increased calf diameter and ultrasound-confirmed haematoma, was a key factor prompting transfer to a higher-level care facility for urgent fasciotomy.

title: Limb ischemia-reperfusion injury in rats is partially mediated by enhancing necroptosis via phosphorylation of RIPK1 and MLKL.
abstract: Limb ischemia-reperfusion injury (L-IRI) causes severe skeletal muscle damage and functional impairment through activation of regulated cell-death and inflammatory pathways. Necroptosis is a regulated form of necrotic cell death mediated through the receptor-interacting protein kinase 1 (RIPK1)-RIPK3-mixed lineage kinase domain-like protein (MLKL) signaling axis. Prior experimental studies have shown that Necrostatin-1 (Nec-1) attenuates acute skeletal muscle ischemia-reperfusion injury in rats. However, how Nec-1-sensitive protection relates to RIPK1/MLKL-associated signaling, circulating muscle injury markers, inflammatory responses, histological damage, and functional recovery during the early postischemic period remains incompletely defined. In this study, we used a rat model of unilateral hindlimb ischemia involving 3 h of ischemia followed by reperfusion for up to 7 days to evaluate these interrelated responses. Nec-1 was administered before ischemia and after reperfusion. L-IRI resulted in elevated plasma creatine kinase and lactate dehydrogenase levels, severe histopathological injury, increased TUNEL staining, impaired grip strength, and reduced Modified Tarlov scores. These changes were accompanied by increased phosphorylation of RIPK1 and MLKL, activation of inflammatory signaling pathways, and altered expression of injury-associated inflammatory mediators. Nec-1 treatment reduced RIPK1/MLKL-associated signaling, inflammatory mediator expression, circulating muscle injury markers, and histological injury while preserving muscle architecture and improving functional recovery. These findings support and extend previous evidence that Nec-1-sensitive necroptosis-associated signaling contributes to early skeletal muscle injury following L-IRI. Pharmacologic targeting of regulated necrotic and inflammatory pathways warrants further investigation as a potential adjunct strategy for limiting acute skeletal muscle injury after limb reperfusion.NEW & NOTEWORTHY This study links Necrostatin-1 (Nec-1)-sensitive receptor-interacting protein kinase 1 (RIPK1)/mixed lineage kinase domain-like protein (MLKL)-associated signaling with biochemical, histological, inflammatory, and functional outcomes after rat hindlimb ischemia-reperfusion injury. Nec-1 reduced RIPK1 and MLKL phosphorylation, muscle injury, and early functional impairment. These findings extend prior skeletal-muscle studies by integrating molecular pathway activation with longitudinal functional recovery while supporting a contribution of RIPK1-associated necroptotic signaling.

title: Immunomodulatory and Antioxidant Biomimetic Hydrogel Coloaded with Glycyrrhizic Acid and Copper Gallate for Synergistic Cartilage Regeneration.
abstract: Articular cartilage lesions are persistently restrained by three interwoven pathological drivers: chronic inflammatory response, sustained oxidative stress, and progressive extracellular matrix (ECM) catabolism. Coupled with the inherently weak self-repair capacity of hyaline cartilage, effective therapeutic interventions for such injuries remain an unmet clinical demand owing to the inherently poor self-repair capacity of hyaline cartilage, effective therapeutic interventions remain an unmet clinical demand. Herein, we engineered a biomimetic composite hydrogel designated ECM/HAMA/GA@Cu-GA, which integrates decellularized cartilage extracellular matrix, methacrylated hyaluronic acid (HAMA), glycyrrhizic acid (GA), and copper gallate (Cu-GA). This integrated hydrogel platform simultaneously endows biomimetic mechanical support, potent anti-inflammatory and antioxidative bioactivities, as well as robust chondrogenic induction capacity. In vitro cellular evaluations verified the outstanding biocompatibility of the composite hydrogel. The biomaterial efficiently polarizes macrophages toward the anti-inflammatory M2 phenotype, suppresses the secretion of pro-inflammatory mediators and matrix-degrading proteases, and facilitates the migration and chondrogenic differentiation of bone marrow mesenchymal stem cells (BMSCs). Transcriptomic profiling suggested that its underlying molecular mechanisms may involve activation of the PI3K/Akt signaling cascade and blockade of the NF-κB-mediated inflammatory pathway. In vivo assessments using rat articular cartilage defect models demonstrated that the ECM/HAMA/GA@Cu-GA hydrogel achieves satisfactory synchronous regeneration of hyaline cartilage and subchondral bone at 4 and 8 weeks post-implantation, with superior regenerative performance relative to all control groups. Collectively, this multifunctional hydrogel enables comprehensive remodeling of the pathological joint microenvironment with favorable biosafety profiles, representing a translatable candidate strategy for clinical management of cartilage degenerative disorders.

title: Satellite Cells as Regulators of the Skeletal Muscle Microenvironment: Evidence Beyond Fusion.
abstract: Wedged between the sarcolemma and basal lamina, satellite cells (SCs) are resident skeletal muscle stem cells responsible for regeneration following injury. SCs share this microenvironment with fibrogenic, immune, vascular, and neural cell populations. Accumulating evidence indicate that SCs do more from this position than regenerate muscle. Activated SCs participate directly in extracellular matrix (ECM) remodeling and signal to fibroblasts and fibro-adipogenic progenitors (FAPs) through miRNA-containing extracellular vesicles (EVs). SCs also reside near capillaries, where reciprocal signaling with endothelial cells stimulates angiogenesis and in return influences myofiber adaptation. SCs are also localized at the neuromuscular junction (NMJ), where they secrete proteins implicated in synaptic remodeling. During regeneration, SCs share their environment with infiltrating immune cells, and while the influence of macrophages on SCs is well established, the reciprocal direction remains comparatively unexplored. EV transport has emerged as one candidate mechanism for part of this influence, operating independently of SC-myofiber fusion. However, supporting evidence is stronger for fibroblasts and FAPs than for endothelial cells and is currently absent for NMJ, immune cells, and non-myogenic fate transitions. The consequences of losing SCs are evident in SC depletion models, where muscle develops excess collagen, blunted capillary expansion, and NMJs that regenerate poorly and degenerate prematurely with age. Whether SCs also transition to fibrogenic or adipogenic fates in aged and dystrophic muscle remains less clear. This review highlights non-canonical roles of SCs and evaluates fusion-independent communication, including SC-derived EVs, as a candidate mechanism linking SCs to the fibrogenic, immune, vascular, and neural compartments of muscle.
journal: American journal of physiology. Cell physiology

title: Ethanol-induced alterations in mesenchymal stromal cells and the effects of aspalathin: implications for alcohol-associated osteonecrosis.
abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Alcohol-associated osteonecrosis is a debilitating condition characterized by progressive bone destruction. Although mesenchymal stromal cells (MSCs) play a critical role in tissue repair, the effects of chronic alcohol exposure on MSCs and their responsiveness to microenvironmental signals remain unclear.
METHODS: MSCs were exposed to ethanol (EtOH) to evaluate changes in viable cell number, ROS-related fluorescence signals, and the expression of mitochondrial-related, senescence-associated, and chemokine signaling-related molecules. CXCL12 expression was examined in human femoral head specimens and ethanol-exposed osteocyte-like cells. The effects of aspalathin (ASP) on EtOH-induced alterations in MSCs were also investigated.
RESULTS: EtOH exposure reduced viable MSC number and increased ROS-related fluorescence signals. It was also associated with decreased expression of ATP5A and CXCR4 and increased expression of p16. CXCL12 expression was higher in alcohol-associated osteonecrosis tissue than in osteoarthritis tissue and appeared qualitatively increased in ethanol-exposed osteocyte-like cells. These findings indicate altered CXCL12 and CXCR4 expression across the tissue and in vitro experimental settings. ASP treatment attenuated the EtOH-induced reduction in the CCK-8 signal, was associated with attenuation of ROS-related fluorescence signals, significantly restored ATP5A expression, suppressed p16 expression, and showed a non-significant trend toward recovery of CXCR4 expression.
CONCLUSIONS: Ethanol exposure was associated with alterations in the cellular state of MSCs, accompanied by changes in ROS-related fluorescence signals and the expression of mitochondrial-related, senescence-associated, and chemokine signaling-related molecules. ASP partially attenuated some of these ethanol-induced alterations. Further studies are required to clarify the functional significance of these findings and to validate them in vivo.

title: Nanofibers based flexible strain sensors.
abstract: The rapid advancement in technology has led to a surge in the development and use of wearable electronics to monitor human health and motion. Wearable sensors have become integral to biomedical monitoring, as they hold immense potential to transform continuous patient assessment and disease management. This has been enabled by the development of stretchable and flexible sensors which can be integrated into electronic devices. Among various wearable sensors, flexible nanofibers-based strain sensors that are capable of detecting movement with high precision and resolution are now receiving signification attention from researchers. Additionally, their non-invasive nature and high wearing comfort further enhance their suitability for biomedical monitoring applications. This review article aims to cover the advances in the development of nanofiber-based strain sensors. Initially, we look at the current state of the broader field of strain sensors, defining their purpose, use, and potential applications. This is followed by a detailed background of various types of strain sensors covering the response mechanisms of resistive and capacitive type sensors. We have provided expansive coverage of various parameters necessary to define the performance of a strain sensor including tensile properties, gauge factor (GF), linearity, response time, recovery time, and durability. We also discuss factors pertinent to biomedical monitoring such as adhesion, biocompatibility, washability, and breathability. Since the focus of this review is on nanofibers-based strain sensors, we describe the various common methods to prepare nanofibers such as electrospinning and nebulization spinning. In addition, a summary of various conducting polymers and composites made from different non-conducting polymeric backbones is provided in this review. Furthermore, their potential applications in biomedical, sports, and virtual reality industries are discussed. Finally, the research gaps which prevent these sensors from commercialization are discussed in the conclusions section along with the scope of future work to ensure the translation of such strain sensors to the market.

title: EMSCs-derived exosomes rescue p75NTR-/- -mediated osteogenesis deficiency via PI3K/Akt/ERK1/2 signaling pathways.
abstract: The repair of the critical-sized bone defects remains a major challenge for orthopedic surgeons, particularly when osteogenesis is impaired by p75 neurotrophin receptor (p75NTR) deficiency. However, the underlying molecular mechanisms are not fully understood. This study aimed to clarify the role of p75NTR in bone regeneration and to develop a cell-free approach to rescue p75NTR-/- deficiency-mediated osteogenic deficiency through a controlled releasing of wild-type ectomesenchymal stem cells exosomes (WT-Exo) which were incorporated into silk fibroin/polycaprolactone2:5/polyvinyl alcohol (SF/PCL2:5/PVA) coaxial nanofibrous membranes. p75NTR-/- mice exhibited a reduced bone mass and delayed ossification, while WT-Exo-loaded membranes partially restored osteogenic deficiency in p75NTR-/- cells and enhanced expression of osteogenic markers such as alkaline phosphatase (ALP), collagen type I (Col-I), osteopontin (OPN) and runt-related transcription factor 2 (Runx2) aaccompanied by activating of phosphoinositide 3-kinase (PI3K)/protein kinase B (Akt)/extracellular signal-regulated kinase 1/2 (ERK1/2) signaling pathway. Following implantation of the WT-Exo-loaded membranes into the critical-sized cranial defects in p75NTR-/- mice, new bone formation in the defect site was significantly improved by a sustained release of WT-Exo. Overall, the findings in this study highlighted the critical role of p75NTR in osteogenic differentiation of ectomesenchymal stem cells (EMSCs) and demonstrated that WT-Exo, delivered via the coaxial electrospun membranes, represented an effective cell-free intervention method to reverse bone formation deficiency caused by p75NTR deficiency, providing a promising strategy for gene deficiency-related bone diseases.

title: Advancing regenerative biomaterials and translational strategies in orthopaedic traumatology.
abstract: The 2025 Orthopaedic Trauma Association's Basic Science Focus Forum featured a symposium on regenerative biomaterials and translational strategies for orthopaedic trauma. Four experts presented complementary perspectives on the next generation of bone and soft tissue repair: Dr. J. Tracy Watson described how orthobiologics and refined spacer design can be used to engineer a better Masquelet induced membrane; Dr. Lauren Priddy presented evidence that hydroxyapatite coatings can mitigate the rapid degradation of additively manufactured magnesium scaffolds; Dr. Vaida Glatt described the development and clinical translation of the Biomimetic Hematoma scaffold for bone and muscle regeneration; and Dr. Katherine Hixon outlined how the 3R principles (Replacement, Reduction, Refinement) can serve as a framework to accelerate musculoskeletal regenerative engineering. Collectively, the symposium underscored a shift toward biologically informed, clinically predictive, and ethically responsible engineering solutions for the patients who sustain musculoskeletal trauma.

title: Metabolic Bone Health in Female Patients: Focus on Foot and Ankle.
abstract: Metabolic bone health is crucial for the overall well-being of female patients. Female athletes and young females are of particular interest, as their skeletal systems are still developing and are sensitive to the hormonal and physical stress of training and diet. Stress fractures occur with higher frequency in females with risk factors such as low bone mineral density (BMD). When low bone mineral density occurs along with menstrual irregularities and relative energy deficiency, it completes the female triad (23, 27, and 28). Any discussion of female BMD and metabolic bone health must include the female triad.

title: Adhesive hydrogel-mediated spatiotemporal delivery of garlic-derived nanovesicles reprograms immunometabolism to rescue periodontal bone regeneration.
abstract: The core challenge in regenerating inflammatory bone defects, such as periodontitis-related bone resorption, lies in the dysregulation of the immune-metabolic microenvironment, which required implanted materials to simultaneously possess tissue sealing properties, sustained immune modulation capacity and metabolic intervention functions. Herein, garlic-derived exosome-like nanovesicles (GaELNs), exhibiting anti-inflammatory and immunomodulatory activities, are embedded in an injectable, tissue-adhesive polyethylene glycol hydrogel (GaE-PEG) to meet the challenges. The hydrogel exhibited favorable tissue adhesion and sustained release of GaELN-associated protein in vitro. GaE-PEG promoted macrophage polarization toward an anti-inflammatory M2 phenotype and reduced pro-inflammatory cytokine expression. In lipopolysaccharide-stimulated periodontal ligament stem cells, GaE-PEG alleviated mitochondrial oxidative stress, restored oxidative phosphorylation, suppressed excessive glycolysis, and enhanced osteogenic differentiation. Transcriptomic and metabolomic analyses linked these effects to mitochondrial metabolic regulation, while oligomycin treatment attenuated the osteogenic response, supporting a contribution of oxidative phosphorylation. In a rat model of periodontitis-related bone defects, GaE-PEG reduced local inflammation and promoted alveolar bone regeneration, with improved regenerative outcomes compared with a single local injection of free GaELNs at an equivalent dose and Bio-Gide™/Bio-Oss™ treatment. These findings support an adhesive hydrogel strategy integrating local nanovesicle delivery with immunomodulation and metabolic regulation to promote bone regeneration under inflammatory conditions.

title: Effects of Intramuscular Mesenchymal Stem Cell and Boric Acid Administration on Muscle Damage and Recovery in an Exhaustive Swimming Rat Model.
abstract: Exhaustive exercise induces damage to skeletal muscle, reducing athletic performance and delaying recovery. Effective experimental strategies are needed to mitigate this damage and accelerate tissue regeneration. This study aimed to address limitations in the therapeutic efficacy of bone marrow-derived mesenchymal stromal/stem cell-like cells (MSCs) associated with limited cell viability by evaluating boric acid (BA) as an antioxidant and metabolic modulator to enhance cell viability and muscle repair. Twenty-five female Wistar albino rats underwent a 15 day exhaustive swimming protocol and received intramuscular injections of MSCs (1 × 106 cells), BA (10 µg), or their combination, according to the experimental group allocation. Bone marrow obtained from five additional donor rats was used exclusively for MSC isolation and culture. Daily exhaustion time, serum biomarkers lactate, lactate dehydrogenase (LDH), creatine kinase (CK), and gastrocnemius histology were evaluated. Intramuscular BA improved endurance and reduced biochemical markers of muscle injury, whereas MSC application promoted structural muscle regeneration, as evidenced by centrally located nuclei and improved muscle fiber integrity. Combined MSCs + BA treatment improved several biochemical and histological outcomes compared with exercise alone. Serum lactate concentrations remained elevated in treated groups 24 h after the final exercise session, indicating altered post-exercise metabolic responses. Overall, intramuscular BA modulated metabolic responses, whereas administration of bone marrow-derived stromal/stem cell-like cells was associated with structural regeneration in this rat model of exercise-induced skeletal muscle injury, providing a reproducible platform for evaluating regenerative interventions.

title: Early Diagnosis and Therapeutic Evaluation of Rheumatoid Arthritis by a Mitochondria-Targeted Near-Infrared Fluorescent Probe.
abstract: As a chronic autoimmune inflammatory ailment, rheumatoid arthritis (RA) presents with persistent synovitis and progressive destruction of cartilage and bone structures, for which early diagnosis and real-time evaluation of therapeutic responses remain significant clinical challenges. Dysregulation of the inflammatory microenvironment, especially mitochondrial dysfunction accompanied by abnormal elevation of mitochondrial viscosity, is closely associated with RA progression. However, current imaging techniques are still insufficient for real-time visualization of these subcellular changes during disease development and treatment. Herein, we present a mitochondria-targeted near-infrared fluorescent probe, YJ-1, constructed based on a donor-π-acceptor (D-π-A) framework for sensitive detection of viscosity variations and dynamic RA imaging. YJ-1 exhibits excellent selectivity toward viscosity changes, efficient mitochondrial localization, and a strong near-infrared emission at 764 nm, enabling high-contrast and low-background imaging. Moreover, the probe demonstrates outstanding photostability, low cytotoxicity, and good biocompatibility. Owing to these advantages, YJ-1 enables real-time visualization of mitochondrial viscosity changes in living cells, zebrafish, and mouse models. In addition, in a λ-carrageenan-induced inflammatory mouse model, YJ-1 successfully monitors disease-associated mitochondrial viscosity alterations and dynamically evaluates mesenchymal stem cell (MSC)-mediated immunoregulatory therapy. Collectively, YJ-1 provides a robust imaging platform for exploring mitochondrial microenvironment dynamics during RA progression and offers a promising strategy for assessing therapeutic efficacy in inflammatory diseases.
